newsitem.title: GERMANY: Protesting Delta staff go on hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Protesting Delta staff go on hunger strike.

text.p: Five Delta Air Lines staff have entered a third day on hunger strike in protest at large-scale job cuts in Frankfurt, a union official said on Wednesday.
Four men and one woman were camping out in front of Delta check-in counters at Frankfurt airport and refusing food, the airline's works council chairman, Walter Czogalla, said.
Conflict between the airline and staff was escalating as Delta pressed ahead with plans to cut staff from 850 to 250 in Frankfurt and drop eight of its 14 daily flights, he warned.
Delta announced in January it would drop unviable flights from Frankfurt to six European cities and three US destinations by the end of June with up to 600 job losses.

Czogalla told Reuters that walkouts by staff this week, including a protest by several hundred employees in Terminal 2 on Tuesday, had delayed flights by up to two and a half hours and affected 2,200 passengers.
Delta had now flown in "strike-breakers" who could take over handling operations during walkouts.

The works council wants job guarantees for the 250 remaining staff and wants Delta to invest 180 million marks, or its expected financial improvement from the restructuring measures, in a social plan valid until 2003, Czogalla said.
Delta's Germany sales manager, Roland Weil, told Reuters the airline was ready to talk with the works council.
But he added: "The works council is demanding almost 250,000 marks per employee and that is not acceptable."
No passengers had been left stranded during walkouts and the delays had been for "acceptable" lengths of time, he said.
Weil added: "We are considering whether it is viable to maintain self-handling at Frankfurt. We are talking with FAG and ground handling companies and evaluating it."
Czogalla said Delta planned to outsource its aircraft handling to Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG) and Rutges BV, and hand over cabin cleaning to cleaning company ASG.
He also said Delta planned to transfer its reservations office with 120 staff from Frankfurt to London, a plan Weil denied.
